set.body:
Plan: docs/plans/2026-09-18-best-recall-to-video-mapper.md §3 Phase 2 Declared decoders.

About 24.5 of Sherlock's 30.4-point gain comes from MonotoneScene, which lives in bench code configured by environment variables and calls itself 'fitted to this corpus'. Fill gains 6.8 on Sherlock and costs 14.0 on FilmFestival.

Scope:
Move the decoder into a library module with its configuration as data.

Acceptance criteria:
1. MonotoneScene lives in a library module with a versioned decoder config (backward penalty, forward-skip penalty, fill) expressed as data.
2. Fill defaults to off.
3. Per-corpus decoder settings are read from the corpus descriptor, not environment variables.
4. Parity: with Sherlock's recorded config the decoder reproduces the all17-monofill anchors byte-identically.
5. Decoder identity and config hash appear in every receipt.

Gate (AGENTS.md SD2/SD6): `sbt -batch clean compileAll testAll` on the merge result, then
`sbt -batch scalafmtCheckAll scalafmtSbtCheck` as a separate run; every test task in build.sbt's
testAll alias reports bound totals (56 at 0e36a7fa, after the corpus modules were added; recount if
modules change); a named mutation witness per new guard, and each compile-time-probe mutation proved
after its own clean recompile; `cd docs-site && npm run verify:examples` when public API or examples
change; fresh-context cold review in a separate pass; the commit body states the evidence and what
it does not establish.

Size: M.
set.title: Phase 2: declared, versioned decoders in the library (MonotoneScene generalised; fill off by default)
